author: Jon Draeger
title: DCNR helps open new trail in Warriors Path State Park - NewsBreak
text:
By Jon Draeger ,
7 hours ago
SAXTON, Pa. (WTAJ) — Broad Top Township supervisors, along with members of the state’s Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, officially opened up a new intercounty trail in the region.
The Huntingdon and Broad Top Rail Trail finished up with a ribbon-cutting to put a bow on the 15-year-long project that took six phases to put together. Funded by community grants, PennDOT and DCNR, the $2.2 million project spans 13.5 miles around the peninsula of Warriors Path State Park, with engineering and consulting done by Mackin Engineering and GAI Consultants.
The path now opens up opportunities for residents to safely explore the scenic landscape, whether on foot or by bike. In turn, the new path has seen high numbers of visitors since it opened.
Fall foliage expected early in Pennsylvania due to dry weather “There was really no place for them to walk, either on the main road and it was unsafe,” Broad Top Township supervisor Donnie Hedge said. “It didn’t work.”
“People meet each other and talk to each other on the trail. It builds health and wellness,” DCNR Secretary Cindy Adams Dunn said. “The visitation to the park increased 47% when the trail was done. It’s something that draws people outside.”
The project was completely done by the Broad Top Township supervisors, from planning to paving the walkway. The plan was to help build up assets in outdoor recreation that Bedford County is continuing to invest in.
“We understand that outdoor recreation is a huge part of the quality of life in Bedford County,” Kellie Goodman-Shaffer, the president of the Bedford County Chamber of Commerce, said. “It’s one of the reasons why people want to live here. It’s one of the reasons why people do business here.”
Outdoor recreation in Pennsylvania is a $19 billion industry. Adding more options to a rural area can provide the local economy with a bigger boost and add more residents to the area.
“There are direct jobs that will spring up as a result of this ability and the result of this addition to the recreation offerings of this area,” Adams Dunn said.
The more people who come here to use the trails, the more they tend to buy things from our businesses. They stay in our hotels, they eat in our restaurants,” Goodman-Shaffer added.

With the trail lying ahead for visitors and residents, the potential to see lasting benefits awaits the supervisors. But for now, they see the current aid that the new trail provides.
“It’s going to be a monetary improvement to help some,” Hedge said. “But just the health and welfare of our citizens was our major goal.”
